articles.title: Govt fixes deadlines for 6,000 PM Package flats; Rs 82.45 Cr Migrant Camp renovation to start shortly
articles.description: Srinagar, Sep 16: A meeting to review the ongoing and new projects of Department of Disaster Management, Relief, Rehabilitation & Reconstruction (DMRR&R) was held under the joint chairmanship of Anil Kumar Singh, Additional Chief Secretary, PW(R&B) Department and Chandraker Bharti, Principal Secretary, DMRR&R. The meeting was attended by the Relief & Rehabilitation Commissioner (M), J&K, Chief Engineers PW(R&B) North/Central/South Kashmir, Chief Engineer KPDCL, Chief Engineer PW(R&B) Jammu and senior officers from the Public Works Department, DMRR&R, Jal Shakti Department and Divisional Administration Kashmir. It was informed that out of 6,000 flats approved for accommodation of PM Package employees at 20 locations across Kashmir Valley, 5,176 flats have been completed. Besides, allied works including installation of lifts, internal roads, drainage and community halls are also nearing completion at most sites. Specific deadlines for completion of balance works and handover/takeover were fixed, with directions to hand over the possession of completed flats to the eligible employees in a phased manner as per allotments already made under the government norms. Regarding major repair and renovation of various blocks at migrant camps in Jammu, for which the government has approved Rs 82.45 crore, it was informed that tender formalities have been completed and work is likely to start shortly. Meanwhile, directions were also issued for finalization of a detailed project for upgradation of infrastructure in the migrant schools, health dispensaries, internal roads and parks in the migrant camps. Likewise, an extensive review of construction of PoJK Bhawan at Suketar was also held with emphasis on completing the project in all respects within the current financial year. The Chief Engineer, PW(R&B) Jammu apprised the meeting that the DPR for construction of additional flats for Kashmiri migrants at Purkhoo, Jammu is being finalized and the Multipurpose Community Hall at Jagti with an estimated cost of Rs 6.50 crore has been completed. It was further informed that for new projects with an approximate financial implication of Rs 20.00 crore at migrant camps Purkhoo, Nagrota, Muthi and Jagti in the current financial year, tender formalities are in progress. Besides, DPRs are being prepared for the new projects proposed for next financial year, including E-Learning Centres, Digital Libraries and Reading Rooms, Career Counselling and Guidance Centres, Skill Development and Vocational Training Centres, Entrepreneurship Facilitation Centres, Sports Infrastructure and Solar Power/Water Conservation projects in migrant camps.

articles.title: No vacancy in Estates’ 1608 units
articles.description: Srinagar, Sep 16: Despite having 1608 government accommodation units Kashmir Division, the Jammu and Kashmir Estates Department has still engaged 78 hotels and guest houses for the 2026 summer session. The Department has stated that no accommodation it manages is vacant at the moment reflecting the pressure on government-operated and owned buildings in J&K. Seven quarters have been allotted to political parties, the RTI has stated. It said that no government accommodation was occupied illegally by employees or political leaders. The department refused details of accommodation allotted to social activists, journalistsand political leaders in J&K citing security grounds. “In view of the prevailing security and law and order situation in the Jammu and Kashmir, disclosure of details relating to accommodation allotted to social activists, journalists and political leaders including location, particulars and other details of such accommodation many have security implications,” the RTI reply reads. These figures have been disclosed by the Department as a reply to an application filed by M M Shuja. As per the response, the total budget allocated to the Directorate of Estates (Jammu) and Directorate of Estates (Kashmir) from March 2025 to March 2026 was Rs 61 crore. The department spent Rs 58.43 crore. The Estates Department, Kashmir, has 1608 accommodation units under its control, the RTI reply states. None of the accommodations is vacant. The only two accommodations vacant in Kashmir division are two Type-VI category and Type-VII special bungalows at Tulsi Bagh. Despite the massive government accommodation infrastructure, the department has taken over 78 hotels and guest houses for the 2026 summer session. The hotels and guest houses are selected through an Expression of Interest and tender process, the RTI states. The department has said that police personnel are deployed at each of these accommodations for frisking and security. The government employees are allotted accommodation in the selected hotels and guest houses after the government appointed committee is satisfied with the standards of the accomodation. In the past six years, the department has constructed 192 flats at Sempora, Pampore. These comprise 16 one-BHK, 112 two-BHK and 64 three-BHK flats. In addition, a multi-storeyed building comprising four three-BHK flats is also coming up at Jawahar Nagar. This is being built on the space where a two-storey building with two government quarters existed but was gutted two years ago. This is also the first multi-storey building in the area where two storey government quarters abound. On the revenue side, Estates Kashmir generated Rs 19.24 crore between 2020-21 and 2025-26, with annual revenue standing at Rs 2.11 crore in 2020-21, Rs 3.32 crore in 2021-22, Rs 2.27 crore in 2022-23, Rs 3.47 crore in 2023-24, Rs 4.70 crore in 2024-25 and Rs 3.55 crore in 2025-26. However, Rs 2.68 crore remain outstanding licence fee (update of June 30, 2026).

articles.title: Leh Workshop Helps MSMEs Explore Public Procurement, Finance And Export Opportunities
articles.description: Leh Workshop Helps MSMEs Explore Public Procurement, Finance And Export Opportunities Leh, Sep 16 (KNN) A national-level workshop in Leh on Tuesday familiarised local entrepreneurs and artisans with public procurement, Government e-Marketplace (GeM) onboarding, quality certification, financing and export promotion opportunities available to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). The one-day workshop was aimed at helping businesses access government procurement opportunities, improve product quality and packaging, secure institutional finance and explore national and international markets. Focus On Government Procurement And Quality The technical sessions covered MSME Ministry schemes, vendor registration and public procurement procedures, including presentations by officials from GeM, NSIC and POWERGRID. Representatives from the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) and Quality Council of India (QCI) briefed participants on BIS certification, Zero Defect, Zero Effect (ZED), Quality Control Orders and quality requirements for public procurement. The Indian Institute of Packaging (IIP) also conducted a session on packaging, highlighting its relevance to market access and exports. Entrepreneurs Briefed On Finance, Exports The workshop also covered export promotion, with officials from the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) outlining opportunities and procedures for exporters. SIDBI officials briefed participants on financing schemes, while the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) highlighted credit-linked financing through the Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) portal. The session also covered value addition and infrastructure upgradation for key Ladakh products, including pashmina, apricot and seabuckthorn. Push For Local Products To Reach Wider Markets Administrative Secretary, Industries and Commerce Department, UT Ladakh, Himanshu Gupta, highlighted MSME schemes including the Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme and PMEGP. He also said the UT Administration was exploring a credit scheme to support aspiring entrepreneurs. Director, Planning, Tsewang Gyalson, urged local entrepreneurs to leverage Ladakh’s resources and explore national and international markets for locally produced goods. The workshop also stressed the importance of Udyam Registration for accessing MSME schemes and encouraged entrepreneurs to regularly use official online portals to stay updated on government programmes. The workshop was organised by the MSME Development and Facilitation Office (MSME-DFO), Jammu, under the Ministry of MSME. (KNN Bureau)
